item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02500","case1_error":"Evaluates Anna’s correctly specified 14 × 60 candy total as 252 instead of 840.","case2_error":"Evaluates the correct expression 180 − 45 − 45 − 20 as 90 instead of 70.","reason":"Both incorrectly evaluate a correctly written arithmetic expression.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J02501","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final profit 88 after the correct formula (16 × 8) − 30, which yields 98.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final earnings 6351 after the correct formula (453 × 12) + (126 × 7), which yields 6318.","reason":"Both supply an incorrect final number after a correct formula without showing the calculation responsible.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J02502","case1_error":"Substitutes one Monday counting session for the two Tuesday tile-counting sessions, producing 1 + 3.","case2_error":"Omits the 250 papers per day multiplier, calculating recycling proceeds for only one paper per day.","reason":"The first explicitly substitutes a count from the wrong day; the second omits the daily quantity multiplier.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02503","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as costing 70% of the original price instead of 30%.","case2_error":"Writes H − F = 21 despite Farah having the higher score; the relation should be F − H = 21.","reason":"Confusing a discount with the remaining price differs from reversing the direction of a stated score comparison.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02504","case1_error":"Leading answer marker says 20, but the correct derivation and concluding answer give 16.","case2_error":"Leading answer marker says 1000, but the correct derivation and concluding answer give 1250.","reason":"Both exhibit only answer-marker conflicts; neither derivation contains a mathematical error.","judgment":"uncertain"}]}
